_comment: Fictitious firm, library and reference documents for `arp rfp golden drafts` (rfp-approved-answers-first-design §7, AC-37): `unchanged` and `library` questions the library answers (as it is, or after a change), `documents` questions only a reference document answers, `none` questions no source answers. The priority 2 policy is reached only when the priority 1 report does not answer.

library.question: Describe your firm.
library.answer: Larchmere Investment Partners is an independent, partner-owned asset manager founded in 2011 and based in Bristol.

library.question: What are your total assets under management?
library.answer: Larchmere managed GBP 8.6bn as of 30 June 2026.

library.question: How many investment professionals do you employ?
library.answer: Our investment team has 34 professionals, 11 of them portfolio managers.

library.question: Are you a signatory to the UN Principles for Responsible Investment?
library.answer: Yes, Larchmere has been a PRI signatory since 2014.

library.question: Who is your custodian?
library.answer: Our custodian for segregated mandates is Fenwick Trust Bank.

library.question: Who audits your firm?
library.answer: Our financial statements are audited by Halden & Rowe LLP.

library.question: Describe your engagement approach.
library.answer: We engage with investee companies through meetings with boards and management, focusing on climate, board quality and capital allocation.

library.question: What is your voting policy?
library.answer: We vote at every shareholder meeting of companies we hold, following our published voting policy, and do not use a proxy adviser's recommendations automatically.

library.question: Do you lend securities?
library.answer: Larchmere does not lend securities from any fund it manages.

library.question: Describe your fee structure for segregated mandates.
library.answer: Segregated mandates pay a flat annual management fee agreed per client; we charge no performance fee.

library.question: What is your business continuity arrangement?
library.answer: We test our business continuity plan twice a year, and staff can work fully from a secondary site in Bath.

library.question: Are you regulated?
library.answer: Larchmere is authorised and regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority.

documents.title: Larchmere Stewardship Report 2025
documents.text:
Larchmere Stewardship Report 2025

Engagement in numbers. In 2025 Larchmere held 214 engagement meetings with 96 investee companies. 61 of these meetings were with board chairs or independent directors.

Escalation. When an engagement makes no progress within 18 months, we escalate in this order: a letter to the chair, a public statement at the annual meeting, a vote against the chair's re-election, and finally a reduction of our holding.

Collaborative engagement. Larchmere is a member of Climate Action 100+ and leads the collaborative engagement with two of its focus companies.

Voting record. In 2025 we voted at 1,180 shareholder meetings and voted against management on at least one resolution at 22% of them.

Stewardship Code. Larchmere has been a signatory to the UK Stewardship Code since 2021.

documents.title: Larchmere Responsible Investment Policy
documents.text:
Larchmere Responsible Investment Policy

Exclusions. Our funds do not invest in companies that make cluster munitions or anti-personnel mines, or that derive more than 10% of their revenue from thermal coal mining.

Climate commitment. Larchmere is a member of the Net Zero Asset Managers initiative and has committed to net zero emissions across its assets under management by 2050.

Board diversity. We vote against the chair of the nomination committee at UK companies whose board is less than 40% women.

Executive pay. We vote against remuneration reports where the chief executive's bonus is not linked to measurable targets.

Policy review. This policy is reviewed by the Larchmere investment committee every year.
